subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 03, 2026
body:
Our continuous integration pipeline just got another boost with the introduction of per-pipeline staging directories, significantly reducing the likelihood of publish races between concurrent builds, and the use of relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, ensuring it resolves correctly on the host web root. This refinement is part of our ongoing effort to enhance the reliability and stability of our ISO build process, which you can track on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Development 
The recent updates to our CI pipeline demonstrate the community's commitment to streamlining our release process, making it easier for users to get the latest version of AcreetionOS. Our focus on enhancing our CI pipeline is driven by the need for a robust and reliable release process, which is critical for an Arch-based distribution like AcreetionOS. For more information on our development process, you can visit our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html.

Community 
The AcreetionOS community has been actively engaged in discussions around the latest Emacs 31.1 release and the security updates issued by AlmaLinux. These conversations highlight the community's interest in staying up-to-date with the latest developments in the Linux ecosystem. If you're interested in learning more about AcreetionOS and its community, you can visit our website at https://acreetionos.org/ and explore our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html. Tip of the day: you can also check out our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html for the latest news and updates.
